title: UPDATE: Canadian Credit Market Hit by Spreading Global AI Debt Selloff

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock
Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
Increased borrowing by Alphabet and other cloud providers is triggering a selloff of AI-related debt in Canada, leaving the smaller credit market more vulnerable to swings in foreign debt valuation. The pressure stems from a global surge in bond offerings by the companies known as hyperscalers, which are raising capital to fund massive expansions in artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The scale of the borrowing has intensified recently, with Microsoft, Meta, and Oracle arranging more than $60B in new bonds in a single week, including a $25B issuance from Microsoft. This activity helped push total global bond sales to an all-time high of $6.61T this year, with the collective debt raised by the hyperscaler group reaching $271B. While BlackRock's Rick Rieder called the current fixed-income landscape attractive, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said the volume of hyperscaler debt has contributed to rising bond yields.

These are the smartest and most financially stable companies in the world, and they can see across the entire tech and infrastructure sector better than any analyst ever could

If one of them was doing this, you could debate it. But when every single hyperscaler is doing the exact same thing at the same time, it's really hard to bet against them

Conclusion: we are going higher, the market just doesn't believe it yet
